**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَالَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَمْرُهُمْ شُورَىٰ بَيْنَهُمْ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ﴾

And those who answered their Lord when He called them to His Oneness and obedience to Him, and established the obligatory prayer properly at its times; when they want to do something, they consult one another about it; and from the wealth We have given them they give in charity in the way of Allah, and they pay the rights Allah has made obligatory on them to those entitled to them, of zakah, spending on family, and other kinds of spending.

﴿وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ ۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ﴾

… And consult them in matters that need consultation; then when you have decided on something — after consulting — carry it out relying on Allah alone. Allah loves those who rely on Him.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Uncle Arif say to Abu Maher before he left the old road? And how did Abu Maher answer him? And what did they find at the well?
2. What did Abu Maher say to the men of the caravan around the fire? And why was saying "I made a mistake" courage and not weakness?
3. Basil was the youngest in the caravan, so why did Abu Maher ask him? And does consultation mean always doing what most people say? (No; consultation is listening to all the opinions, and then the one in charge decides on the soundest of them and relies on Allah, just as Abu Maher put Basil's observation together with Uncle Arif's experience.)

**This week's exercise**
This week, hold a family "shura council" about something real (where to go on the Friday outing, or what to have for dinner): everyone gives their opinion, starting with the youngest, then the decision is made, and the children are told why it was chosen.
